question.problem: Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =0.$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =0.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-6{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
